summary.bn: দুটো D ফ্লিপ-ফ্লপ: ক্লকের প্রতি উঠতি ধারে D-এর মান মনে রাখে
summary.en: Two D flip-flops: each remembers D on every rising edge of its clock

simplified: Each flip-flop answers at once: the few nanoseconds a real one takes, and its set-up and hold times, are left out.
Q takes D when the clock goes from LOW to HIGH. CLR and PRE work at once, whatever the clock does; both LOW make Q and Q̅ both HIGH, as the datasheet's function table says.
Without power it forgets what it held, and starts with Q LOW. A real chip starts with Q either way.

An input is HIGH above 70 % of the supply and LOW below 30 %; in between it keeps its last level. An output is the supply or ground through about 50 Ω. These are typical datasheet figures, not measured.
It is placed across the centre gap with pin 1 at the bottom left, and cannot be turned round.
